status: PROVISIONAL. v2 drafted 2026-10-08 from Hunter's own theory library (Are.na 'informative-pdfs'), replacing v1's placeholder-driven axes (togetherness, cinematic, Boym). Unvalidated until checked against his hand labels. Edit freely; anchors are embedded at scoring time, so no re-embedding is needed.
method: Each axis has two poles written as descriptions of what the PICTURE shows (the model saw silent frames at 1 fps, 360p). Score = mean cosine(clip, high anchors) - mean cosine(clip, low anchors), z-scored across the archive. Scores rank clips against each other; they are not calibrated units.
stance: Sedgwick, 'Paranoid Reading and Reparative Reading' (in the library): label reparatively. Ask what the clip offers or sustains, not what it exposes. This governs how Hunter rates, not how the model scores.

intensity.theory: Massumi; the register the Affect Theory Reader's introduction (Seigworth & Gregg, 'An Inventory of Shimmers') calls intensity passing between bodies, before it is named as an emotion.
intensity.weakness: 1 fps under-reads motion and there is no audio, so loudness is invisible.
high: a sudden jolt of fast motion, the camera lurching while a body moves hard through the frame
a crowded chaotic scene with flashing lights and people pressed together
a close unsteady shot of something happening right now, too fast to follow
a huge crashing wave or a speeding vehicle filling the frame
low: a still empty room in flat light with nothing moving
a long quiet held shot of an ordinary surface where almost nothing happens
a calm slow view of a motionless landscape
an idle moment of waiting, the camera resting on a ceiling or the floor

front_stage.theory: Goffman, The Presentation of Self in Everyday Life (in the library): front region, where a performance is given for an audience, versus back region, where the performer drops the act. Phone video constantly toggles between the two.
front_stage.replaces: v1 'togetherness'. Whether people are performing for the lens is visible; whether they are friends is not.
front_stage.weakness: A mirror selfie and a staged group pose both read as front stage; the axis does not say what the performance is for.
high: a person looking straight into the phone camera, posing, aware of being filmed
friends posing together for the camera, arranged, smiling on cue
someone filming themselves in a mirror, adjusting hair or clothes, checking the frame
a person performing, dancing or lip-syncing toward the lens
low: people caught unaware, not looking at the camera, absorbed in what they are doing
a candid glimpse of someone from behind or from the side, unposed
a scene with no people, filmed as a record of a place
someone asleep or slumped, unguarded, not performing

dwelling.theory: Csikszentmihalyi & Rochberg-Halton, The Meaning of Things: Domestic Symbols and the Self (in the library): the home and its cherished objects as carriers of the self. The low pole is the non-place Hunter named as his own subject on 2026-09-23 ('my Fisher-ian non-space'): transit, retail, screens, interchangeable interiors.
dwelling.replaces: v1 had nothing here. This is the axis a personal phone archive most obviously carries.
dwelling.weakness: A friend's home and a hotel room can look alike at 360p. The axis reads furnishing and personal objects, not ownership.
high: a lived-in bedroom with personal belongings, clothes on the floor, a messy desk, a familiar bed
a kitchen or living room with someone cooking or lounging, objects that clearly belong to them
a pet on a sofa, a cluttered shelf of personal things, a window of a home
a cosy interior with a lamp on, someone at ease in their own space
low: an airport terminal, a parking garage or a hotel corridor, anonymous and interchangeable
a freeway at night from inside a car, signs and lights passing
a mall, a chain store interior or a gas station under flat fluorescent light
a blank waiting room or lobby with nobody who belongs there

poor_image.theory: Steyerl, 'In Defense of the Poor Image' (The Wretched of the Screen, in the library): the low-resolution, compressed, copied-and-recopied image as its own class, whose degradation records circulation and intimacy rather than failure. The phone proxy is a poor image by construction.
poor_image.replaces: v1 'cinematic' (pure taste). Steyerl inverts that axis: the rich, high-definition image is the low pole.
poor_image.weakness: IMPORTANT: every clip was transcoded to the same 360p/0.4 Mbps proxy, which flattens much of this axis before the model sees it. What survives is motion blur, low-light noise, screen-recordings, re-filmed screens and blown-out exposure. Treat as a weak axis until the labels say otherwise.
high: a blurry pixelated phone video, noisy in low light, smeared by motion
a video of another screen, a TV or laptop re-filmed with moire and glare
a screen recording or a reposted clip with compression blocks and a watermark
an overexposed washed-out clip with crushed shadows and banding
low: a crisp high-definition image with clean detail and accurate color
a sharp steady well-lit shot with fine texture visible
a professional-looking clip with shallow focus and no noise
a clean bright daylight scene with nothing blurred

danger.theory: Hunter's own axis (2026-10-27): dangerous <-> safe. Named and approved by him, 'just send it'. Danger is not visible; this scores how much a clip LOOKS like danger imagery.
danger.weakness: Overlaps intensity (fast/chaotic reads dangerous) and day/night (a calm dark car ride reads dangerous). Abstract words embed poorly, so poles are written as pictures.
high: a car speeding at night, headlights and streaks of light, the road barely visible
fire or flashing lights in the dark, a crowd pressed together and shoving
standing near a cliff edge or a high rooftop, the ground far below, the camera unsteady
a lurching handheld shot running through a dark place, something about to happen
low: a bed with a sleeping person or a pet curled up in warm daylight
a calm sunlit kitchen or living room, someone relaxed, nothing moving fast
still water or a quiet garden in soft daylight, a steady held shot
friends sitting close and laughing on a sofa, lamp light, nothing threatening

hauntological.theory: Fisher, Ghosts of My Life (in the library; also the --hauntology mode in philm): the persistence of a past whose future never arrived. Lives in the viewer's relation to the clip, not in the pixels, so Hunter labels it and no anchor scores it. Replaces v1's Boym nostalgia axes, which are not in his library.

cruel_optimism.theory: Berlant, 'Cruel Optimism' (Affect Theory Reader, in the library): an attachment to something that is itself the obstacle to flourishing. Not visually legible. Optional label; included because the reader is in the library and it names a recurring shape in personal footage.

punctum.theory: Barthes, Camera Lucida (not in the library, but the --barthes mode is in philm): the detail that pricks the viewer personally. Label-only by definition.

not_used_and_why.happy_objects (Ahmed, Affect Theory Read: promising (bodies oriented toward a shared object) but overlaps front_stage and dwelling; revisit after labels.
not_used_and_why.bleak_joys (Fuller & Goriunova): a composite (joy inside a bleak setting); could be derived later as high intensity x low dwelling rather than scored directly.
not_used_and_why.The Dialectics of Friendship (Porter & T: a sociology of friendship, not an aesthetics; no visual anchor follows from it. Noted because 'friendship' was not only a placeholder: the text is in the library if Hunter wants that axis back.
